name: krbrelayx
highlights: -t — Target to attack, since this is Kerberos, only HOSTNAMES are valid. Example: smb://server:
-tf — File that contains targets by hostname or full URL, one per line
-w — Watch the target file for changes and update target list automatically (only valid with -t
-ip — IP address of interface to bind SMB and HTTP servers
-r — Redirect HTTP requests to a file:// path on SMBSERVER
-l — Loot directory in which gathered loot (TGTs or dumps) will be stored (default: current dir
-f — Format to store tickets in. Valid: ccache (Impacket) or kirbi (Mimikatz format) default: c

flags.name: --help
flags.description: show this help message and exit

flags.name: -debug
flags.description: Turn DEBUG output ON

flags.name: --target
flags.description: Target to attack, since this is Kerberos, only HOSTNAMES are valid. Example: smb://server:445 If unspecified, will store tickets for later use.

flags.name: -tf
flags.description: File that contains targets by hostname or full URL, one per line

flags.name: -w
flags.description: Watch the target file for changes and update target list automatically (only valid with -tf)

flags.name: --interface-ip
flags.description: IP address of interface to bind SMB and HTTP servers

flags.name: -r
flags.description: Redirect HTTP requests to a file:// path on SMBSERVER

flags.name: --lootdir
flags.description: Loot directory in which gathered loot (TGTs or dumps) will be stored (default: current directory).

flags.name: --format
flags.description: Format to store tickets in. Valid: ccache (Impacket) or kirbi (Mimikatz format) default: ccache

flags.name: -codec
flags.description: Sets encoding used (codec) from the target's output (default "utf-8"). If errors are detected, run chcp.com at the target, map the result with https://docs.python.org/2.4/lib/standard- encodings.html and then execute ntlmrelayx.py again with -codec and the corresponding codec

flags.name: -no-smb2support
flags.description: Disable SMB2 Support

flags.name: --wpad-host
flags.description: Enable serving a WPAD file for Proxy Authentication attack, setting the proxy host to the one supplied.

flags.name: --wpad-auth-num
flags.description: Prompt for authentication N times for clients without MS16-077 installed before serving a WPAD file.

flags.name: --ipv6
flags.description: Listen on both IPv6 and IPv4

flags.name: --krbpass
flags.description: Account password

flags.name: --krbhexpass
flags.description: Hex-encoded password

flags.name: --krbsalt
flags.description: Case sensitive (!) salt. Used to calculate Kerberos keys.Only required if specifying password instead of keys.

flags.name: -e
flags.description: File to execute on the target system. If not specified, hashes will be dumped (secretsdump.py must be in the same directory)

flags.name: -c
flags.description: Command to execute on target system. If not specified, hashes will be dumped (secretsdump.py must be in the same directory).

flags.name: --enum-local-admins
flags.description: If relayed user is not admin, attempt SAMR lookup to see who is (only works pre Win 10 Anniversary)

flags.name: --no-dump
flags.description: Do not attempt to dump LDAP information

flags.name: --no-da
flags.description: Do not attempt to add a Domain Admin

flags.name: --no-acl
flags.description: Disable ACL attacks

flags.name: --no-validate-privs
flags.description: Do not attempt to enumerate privileges, assume permissions are granted to escalate a user via ACL attacks

flags.name: --escalate-user
flags.description: Escalate privileges of this user instead of creating a new one

flags.name: --add-computer
flags.description: Attempt to add a new computer account

flags.name: --delegate-access
flags.description: Delegate access on relayed computer account to the specified account

flags.name: --sid
flags.description: Use a SID to delegate access rather than an account name

flags.name: --dump-laps
flags.description: Attempt to dump any LAPS passwords readable by the user

flags.name: --dump-gmsa
flags.description: Attempt to dump any gMSA passwords readable by the user

flags.name: --dump-adcs
flags.description: Attempt to dump ADCS enrollment services and certificate templates info

flags.name: --adcs
flags.description: Enable AD CS relay attack

flags.name: --template
flags.description: AD CS template. Defaults to Machine or User whether relayed account name ends with `$`. Relaying a DC should require specifying `DomainController`

flags.name: --altname
flags.description: Subject Alternative Name to use when performing ESC1 or ESC6 attacks.

flags.name: --victim
flags.description: Victim username or computername$, to request the correct certificate name.
